evidence: src/infrastructure/InMemoryOrderRepository.ts: class InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository, which is an adapter for a domain port and so belongs in infrastructure.
save(order) stores order.toSnapshot() in a private Map. This is persistence, which belongs in infrastructure.
findById/findAll/findByStatus rebuild entities from stored rows through Order.restore(row). This is persistence-side rehydration of stored data.
findByStatus filters on row.status === status. This is a data query by attribute, not a domain rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: InMemoryOrderRepository is an in-memory implementation of the domain-declared OrderRepository port, and every one of its responsibilities is persistence. The class only does four things: it keeps snapshots in a Map, rebuilds entities through Order.restore, turns entities back into snapshots through order.toSnapshot, and runs simple lookups. The status filter in findByStatus is a query by an attribute. It is not a business rule or state-transition rule. The file has no domain invariants, no orchestration logic and no transport or presentation code, so it fits the infrastructure layer.
